subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as the canonical configured-model health check, and what live-probe cost, timeout, concurrency, redaction, and JSON contract should it guarantee?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a new live CLI probe mode affects provider credentials, model choice diagnostics, token/rate-limit behavior, and overlaps related fallback and compatibility-policy proposals.

options.title: Approve Status Probe All
options.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status`, preserve the current default probe behavior, and require docs plus redacted live CLI proof before landing.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback Diagnostics
options.body: Make the fallback-chain command own configured-model probing so users get one diagnostic path for primary and fallback health.

options.title: Defer To Compatibility Policy
options.body: Keep current auth probes unchanged until the broader provider compatibility matrix defines supported model health semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve Status Probe All
recommendation.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status`, preserve the current default probe behavior, and require docs plus redacted live CLI proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current live auth probe surface and has the strongest recent history across models status, provider identity, and docs for this decision.
